title: Schwa — The Unstressed Vowel & Reduced Function Words
objectives: Produce weak forms of function words in connected speech

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner pronounces 'cup of coffee' with full /ɒv/.
💡 Solution: Drill rhythm: CUP-ə-coffee with fast weak 'of'.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Schwa — The Unstressed Vowel & Reduced Function Words
1. Definition: Schwa /ə/ is the most common vowel sound in English, occurring in almost every unstressed syllable.
2. Rule: Any vowel letter (a, e, i, o, u, y) in an unstressed syllable reduces to neutral schwa /ə/. Function words (to, for, of, and, a, the) reduce to schwa in natural sentences.
3. Why? English is a stress-timed language: stressed syllables are long and clear, unstressed syllables compress into schwa.
4. How to recognize? Unstressed syllables in multi-syllable words and unstressed grammar words in sentences.
5. Common examples: about /əˈbaʊt/, sofa /ˈsoʊfə/, banana /bəˈnænə/, president /ˈprɛzədənt/, cup of coffee /kʌp əv ˈkɔːfi/
6. Counter-examples: Stressed function words at end of sentence (What are you looking AT? /æt/ full vowel).
7. Exceptions: Formal citation speech where every word is stressed equally.
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing full vowels in unstressed syllables (*to-day as /tuːdeɪ/ instead of /təˈdeɪ/).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Schwa is LAZY! Relax jaw, mouth, and tongue into neutral 'uh'!
10. Key vocabulary: schwa, vowel reduction, stress-timed, weak form, function words
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟠 B1
13. Associated Visual: 😴 Neutral relaxed face symbol for schwa /ə/.
14. Key Takeaway: Unstressed syllable = Schwa /ə/! Relax your mouth!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: What is the most common vowel sound in English? (Schwa /ə/)
CCQ 2: What happens to function words like 'to' and 'for' in fluent sentences? (They reduce to weak forms with schwa: /tə/, /fər/)
CCQ 3: How is 'a' in 'about' pronounced? (Schwa /əˈbaʊt/)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Identify and pronounce the schwa sound in these words:
🎯 Item: about ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /əˈbaʊt/ (first syllable is schwa)
🎯 Item: banana ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /bəˈnænə/ (first and last syllables are schwa)
🎯 Item: cup of tea ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /kʌp əv tiː/ ('of' reduces to schwa)
